title: "Focus Follows Mouse" focus modes are not compatible with floating widgets on a not-always-visible Panel
line: With focus follows mouse, moving slowly from a floating panel into its open popup no longer closes the popup and hides the panel.
explanation: With floating applets, PopupPlasmaWindow is placed a margin (8 px) away from the panel, and that gap belongs to no surface of plasmashell. With focus follows mouse, a pointer resting in the gap longer than KWin's focus delay focused the window underneath, which deactivated the popup (closing it) and let an auto-hiding panel hide. The popup now owns a transparent child surface whose input region covers exactly that gap (and the gap to nearby screen edges), so the pointer stays on plasmashell while crossing it. This is the same change as the 517132 fix.

commits.message:
plasmaquick/popupplasmawindow: don't let the pointer through popup gaps

Floating popups leave a gap towards the panel and the screen edges, so
clicks there reached the window below and focus follows mouse closed
the popup when crossing it. A transparent child window now covers it.

BUG: 517132
BUG: 489776

media.caption: Master, focus follows mouse, Dodge Windows panel behind a maximized Konsole: Kickoff open (left); after moving up slowly across the gap the popup and panel are gone (right).
Fixed: same slow move, Kickoff stays open and the panel stays shown (right).

review.text: Adds a transparent, input-only child surface that covers the floating-popup gap, so focus follows mouse and clicks never reach the window below. That fixes the cause (the gap belongs to no plasmashell surface) at the right layer, in libplasma's PopupPlasmaWindow, for every popup. The code and the commit are the same as 517132's, so only one of the two should be submitted, with both BUG lines. The verification covers the reported Dodge Windows case and the applets-only floating case.
